title: 1956 AHSME Problem 37
statement: On a map whose scale is \(400\) miles to an inch and a half, a certain estate is represented by a rhombus having a \(60^\circ\) angle. The diagonal opposite \(60^\circ\) is \(\dfrac3{16}\) in. The area of the estate in square miles is:

solutions.text:
The diagonal opposite the \(60^\circ\) angle divides the rhombus into two equilateral triangles, so its length equals the rhombus side. The map scale is \(\frac{800}{3}\) miles per inch, hence the actual side length is \[ \frac3{16}\cdot\frac{800}{3}=50 \] miles. Therefore the rhombus area is \[ \begin{aligned} 50^2\sin60^\circ &=2500\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\ &=1250\sqrt3. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: In a \(60^\circ\) rhombus, the shorter diagonal equals the side length
The scale is \(\frac{800}{3}\) miles per inch, so convert the \(\frac{3}{16}\)-inch side before finding area
